back-in-stock.title: Back in stock
back-in-stock.description: Customers ask to be told when a sold-out variant returns; they get an email when it is in stock again.

disabled.title: The plugin is disabled
disabled.hint: Fix the plugin options in medusa-config.ts and restart Medusa.

back-in-stock.demoMode: Emails are rendered and logged, nothing is sent.

problem.no_inventory_item: Stock-managed but no inventory item is linked: it can never come back in stock. Link an inventory item or turn off "Manage inventory".

wanted.title: Most wanted
wanted.subtitle: Variants ranked by the people waiting for them, per sales channel.
wanted.empty: Nobody is waiting for anything yet.
wanted.emptyFiltered: Nobody is waiting for the chosen products.
wanted.openWaiting: Show the people waiting for this variant

subscriptions.title: Subscriptions
subscriptions.subtitle: Every request, newest first, with the emails it received.
subscriptions.endConfirmText: {{email}} will get no more emails about {{product}}.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Changes here override the values from medusa-config.ts.
settings.minQuantity: Units that count as back in stock
settings.minQuantityHint: A variant is back when at least this many units are available in the sales channel.
settings.delayMinutesHint: After a stock change the plugin waits this long and checks again, so a quickly corrected mistake sends nothing.
settings.minGapHoursHint: The same subscription is not emailed again within this time.
settings.maxNotificationsHint: After this many emails a subscription gets no more.
settings.doubleOptIn: Ask for confirmation by email (double opt-in)
settings.doubleOptInHint: Subscriptions start only after the customer clicks the link in a confirmation email.
settings.endedDays: Remove email from ended subscriptions after (days)
settings.consentHint: Shown next to the form. It must say that emails continue until purchase or unsubscribe. Empty uses the default.
settings.resetText: Every setting goes back to the value from medusa-config.ts. Subscriptions are not affected.

sending.title: Sending
sending.emails: Through the Emails plugin (editable text, send log)
sending.notification: Built-in template through the notification module
sending.demo: Demo mode: rendered and logged only
sending.emailsHint: To send through the Emails plugin, spread backInStockEmailTemplate into its templates option.

demoTools.title: Demo
demoTools.subtitle: Sample subscriptions from your own catalog. Their emails are only rendered and logged, never sent.
demoTools.deleteText: Every demo subscription and its history is deleted. Real subscriptions are not touched.
demoTools.hint: Then use "Simulate restock" on the Most wanted tab with the Demo filter.

widget.title: Back in stock
widget.subtitle: People waiting for each variant
widget.empty: Nobody is waiting for this product.

demoReset.body: Every demo subscription is deleted and a fresh set is created on out-of-stock products: three sample subscribers, five products each. Real subscriptions are not touched and nothing is sent.

guide.title: How back in stock notifications work
guide.subtitle: From "Notify me" on a product to the email when it is back.

start.title: What it does
start.text: Customers ask to be told when a variant is back. When Medusa's inventory shows it can be ordered again, everyone waiting gets one email, and the plugin stops once they buy it, unsubscribe or the request expires.

storefront.title: In the storefront
storefront.text: Show "Notify me" on variants that cannot be ordered and post the email and variant to /store/back-in-stock/subscriptions. Signed-in customers need no email: their account email is used.

consent.title: Consent and double opt-in
consent.text: The consent text shown at subscription is stored with it (Settings). With double opt-in, a confirmation email goes first, and the request counts only once it is confirmed.

restock.title: Detecting a restock
restock.text: Inventory changes trigger a check after delayMinutes, so a quick stock correction sends nothing. Availability is counted the way the store API counts it: only the sales channel's stock locations, stocked minus reserved.

emails.title: Emails
emails.text: With the emails plugin, these emails use its branding, editable text and send log. Without it, a built-in Polish and English template goes through Medusa's notification module. minGapHours and maxNotifications keep anyone from getting too many.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.text: Addresses are used only for these notifications. Every email has an unsubscribe link that never acts just by being opened. Unconfirmed requests are deleted after 7 days; ended ones lose the email after 180 days.

demo.title: Demo mode
demo.text: With demo: true emails are rendered and logged, never sent. "Restore test data" creates sample requests on out-of-stock products, Settings creates them for your own addresses, and the Most wanted tab simulates a restock.

install.title: Install the plugin
install.body: npm install, add it to plugins in medusa-config.ts with backendUrl and run npx medusa db:migrate.

links.title: Set the store links
links.body: storefrontUrl (or urls.confirm and urls.unsubscribe), so links in emails lead to the store.

sending.title: Connect sending
sending.body: With the Emails plugin the messages go through it. Without it, a notification provider must handle the "{{channel}}" channel: check it in medusa-config.ts.

storefront.title: Add "Notify me" in the store
storefront.body: Next to variants that cannot be ordered, POST /store/back-in-stock/subscriptions. Done when the first real subscription arrives.

doubleOptIn.title: Double opt-in
doubleOptIn.body: Settings → "Ask for confirmation by email": the customer first confirms the address by a link in an email.

firstEmail.title: First email
firstEmail.body: Done when the first real "back in stock" email goes out. In demo mode you can simulate a restock on the Most wanted tab.

production.title: Go live
production.body: Demo mode off, so emails really go out.
